findings.en: Render and GitHub take part in the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which the European Commission has recognised as providing an adequate level of protection.
findings.target: Render y GitHub participan en el Marco de Privacidad de Datos UE-EE. UU. (EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework), para el que la Comisión Europea ha reconocido un nivel de protección adecuado.
findings.suggestion: Render y GitHub participan en el Marco de Privacidad de Datos UE-EE. UU. (EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework), que la Comisión Europea ha reconocido como garante de un nivel de protección adecuado.
findings.explanation: «para el que la Comisión Europea ha reconocido un nivel de protección adecuado» is an awkward relative construction (one recognises a framework AS providing protection, not a level FOR it); «que … ha reconocido como garante de un nivel de protección adecuado» reads naturally and keeps the meaning.

findings.explanation: Accuracy nuance (rule 1): the English says the Commission recognised the Framework AS PROVIDING adequate protection; «para el que … ha reconocido un nivel» reads as a level recognised «for» the Framework and blurs who provides the protection. The suggestion restores the «recognised as providing» relation without adding anything. The meaning is broadly kept, so this is a nuance, not a factual change.
findings.rule: fidelity: relation in the source kept

changes.reason: Rubric rule 1 (accuracy) in a legal text: «para el que … ha reconocido un nivel» blurs that the Framework is what provides the adequate protection; the fix restores «recognised as providing». Both reviewers' «garante» was not taken because it adds a guarantee the English does not state (rule 2); «ofrece» matches «providing».
